summary: 1. Key operational findings Oct 16 posted 12,834 BCM against a 12,036.1 BCM target (+6.63%), MTD 449,252 BCM (-6.69% vs target), day 22 of 30 (8 days remaining). 2. Three things to flag: 1. 3. The day's composition is the story, not the total: waste missed by 24.23% (7,440 against 9,818.6 BCM, the cycle's largest waste miss) while ore beat its target by 143.25% (5,394 against 2,217.5 BCM, the cycle's largest ore surplus), with Stage 4 share recovering further to 37.92% -- continuing the gradual return toward Ma'aden's written "Stage 4 first" priority. 4. The general comment "Yesterday was Roster break" explains the smallest absolute daily total this cycle despite the target beat, and accounts for the cluster of 12 h standby entries across the excavator fleet. 2. 5. EX-247's standing low-power/derate fault cleared at 5:30 PM after 12 h down, and for the second day running the Daily Availability Final Report and the Client Meeting Report read the fault identically (12 h, 50.00% avail) -- treating the Oct 14 source conflict as resolved rather than a recurring pattern. 3. 6. DT-109 is logged down the full 24 h for a second day, but today's report calls the fault "Engine Failure" (Engine) where yesterday's called it "No Gear" (Power Train), both dated to the same 15-Oct 11 PM opening with no clearing event between the two reports -- flagged for maintenance to confirm whether this is one incident reclassified or two separate faults. 7. Fleet availability (Daily Availability Final Report, authoritative over the A&U workbook): excavators 77.98% day / 66.91% MTD, up from Oct 15's 75.60%; trucks 93.15% / 90.73%; drills 96.88% / 87.47% -- the cycle's biggest drilling surplus (1,846 m against 1,281.4 m target, +44.06%), after Oct 15's standby-driven miss eased off; overall 97.23% / 88.77%, core fleet 96.17%. 8. Lost volume: excavators (EX-253 full day, EX-247 12 h before clearing, EX-123 1 h) 11,950 BCM / 32,265.0 t at planned rates; dump trucks (DT-107, DT-109, DT-130, DT-246) 3,517.1 BCM / 9,496.1 t at today's 61.17 BCM/h fleet rate. 9. Combined gross 15,467.1 BCM / 41,761.1 t. The Client Meeting Report's own "MTD Actual Survey" cell jumped from 388,268 to 409,572 BCM between the Oct 15 and Oct 16 tabs. By the one-day reporting lag tracked since Oct 9, this is read as the Oct 15 production day's survey figure, even though the standalone 261016-INX-SUM.xlsx workbook has still not landed in RAW on its own. Treated that way, the cumulative survey-versus-trucks gap widens to -26,846 BCM (-6.55% of survey), reversing the narrowing trend running since Oct 13 (Oct 13 -9.69%, Oct 14 -6.14%, now -6.55%). This reading is inferred from the lagged MTD cell, not read from a dated file with its own daily figure and loading-location comment -- flagged in [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] to confirm once the workbook lands. Flag, not resolved (new this pass): two new document families appeared in `Maaden Plans/` -- an ADW Shutdown Preparedness deck/workbook/email set, and an "ADW - 2027 readiness presentation" email in the Q4 Recovery Plans folder. Both registered by name only, not read or compiled. The shutdown-preparedness subject matter overlaps the crusher-shutdown narrative already running in daily-production-report and is worth a dedicated read on a future full compile pass. The A&U, DPR, Drill Meters, Block Info, DPR and A&U docx, Equipment Running Hours, Running Hours Maaden, and Distance Report workbooks gained Oct 16 tabs but were registered by name only, not deep-read (the Client Meeting Report and the Daily Availability Final Report cover the figures compiled this pass). Source: KNOWLEDGE/mining_operations_kb/RAW via the librarian compile protocol.
